title: Dashboard good practice: hierarchy, context and clarity

videos.script: On a Monday morning, a tile on the dashboard says June revenue is down forty-six percent. Somebody calls a meeting. {{tile}} Every number on that tile is correct. And the conclusion is wrong. June has seventeen days of data. May had thirty-one. {{partial}} This lesson is about the gap between a correct number and a correct reading. {{gap}} A dashboard starts from a short list of questions, for one reader, on a known schedule. {{questions}} Every number on it needs a comparison. The right one, which is not always last month. {{context}} A partial month is compared with the same days of the last one. A rate on five orders shows its count. A colour never stands alone. {{rules}} You will build Lantern's Monday page in Metabase. Then you will review it the way its first reader would. {{review}} And June, against the same seventeen days of May, turns out to be down eight percent. A different meeting entirely. {{end}}
